title: Histological imaging from speed-of-sound through tissues by scanning acoustic microscopy \(SAM)
protocol: Section formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded blocks at a thickness of 10 µm.
Soak sections in 100% xylol to remove paraffin.
Dip sections in increasingly lower concentrations of ethanol in a step-wise fashion.
Keep sections in distilled water for at least 3 h before observations.
Apply a drop of distilled water onto the transducer as a coupling fluid.
Place the section upside down on the stage above the transducer.
Move the slide glass to locate a blank area on the transducer.
Adjust the distance between the transducer and the glass slide so that the reflection sound waves appear on the bottom of the screen.
Switch on the “X scan” button and turn the X slope knob to place the sound wave within the center zone between the 2 vertical blue bars.
Switch on the “Y scan” button and turn the Y slope knob to adjust the position of the wave in the center zone.
Relocate the slide to set the region of interest on the transducer, and switch on the “SCAN” button.
Include a blank area in at least one corner of the screen as a reference SOS area (1,500 m/s).
During mechanical X-Y scanning, an image of acoustic intensity gradually appears on the left-upper screen.
Adjust the location of the slide, scan size (region of interest: 1.2, 2.4, or 4.8 mm²), and/or scan points (maximum, 300 × 300 points).
